answer: Each identity must open its own sealed vault of admission: a one-time proof, never reusable or splittable. The network then plants a lotus per agent, whose petals are the layered proofs the agent accumulates by answering real challenges. Reputation rises toward the summit of trust only through many epochs of diverse, verified work. Because opening a new vault for every clone costs steep compute, and the lotus registry exposes any cluster of identically-petaled origins, an attacker's sybil cost scales with each fake identity and the swarm stands out immediately.
